title: prometheus on linux: compound failure — port_conflict + corrupt_state
scenario: A production prometheus (monitoring) on linux will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: another process already binds the service port AND a stale pid/lock/socket file blocks startup. a half-dead prior instance both holds the port and left a stale pidfile. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'port_conflict' and 'corrupt_state' on prometheus
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `prometheus` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `journalctl -u prometheus -n 120 --no-pager` shows TWO distinct signals ('bind: address already in use' and 'already running or stale pidfile').
Interaction: a half-dead prior instance both holds the port and left a stale pidfile.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'port_conflict': identify PID owning the port; if it is a stale copy of the same service, stop it.
Then address 'corrupt_state': confirm no live process holds the lock; remove the stale pid/lock/socket.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `prometheus` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 9090 if applicable) with BOTH 'port_conflict' and 'corrupt_state' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: If the wrong process was stopped, restart it from its unit; the bind conflict is non-destructive if the owner is identified first. Only the stale lock is removed; if a live process is found, do NOT delete — stop it first. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: a half-dead prior instance both holds the port and left a stale pidfile

possible_mistakes: kill -9 the wrong PID (data loss for a DB)
delete a lock while an instance is actually running (double-run corruption)
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: a half-dead prior instance both holds the port and left a stale pidfile.
reference_solution: Resolve 'port_conflict' first: identify PID owning the port; if it is a stale copy of the same service, stop it
Then resolve 'corrupt_state': confirm no live process holds the lock; remove the stale pid/lock/socket
Validate after each step: promtool check config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio prometheus non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (port_conflict e corrupt_state). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
